thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing token cross-contamination between concurrent user sessions in prod-nyc. Happens on long contexts (>30k tokens). Low rate but reproducible locally with long convo replay. Example below.

alex: Can you paste a short repro and logs? Which model + runtime path?

maya: Model: rwd/open-13b-8k (quantized path), runtime: v2.14.3. Repro steps: run two parallel chats, feed user B a large system prompt + long history, then send user A a short prompt — A's response sometimes contains a trailing fragment from B. Attaching trimmed log where KV pages look suspicious.

maya: ```
KV pages: [page=117, offset=4096, len=2048, epoch=42, ref=1]
KV pages: [page=118, offset=0, len=4096, epoch=43, ref=0]
-- serve(req=abcd): read_block(page=118, off=0) -> tokens 0..127
-- after serve(req=abcd): page=118 start_offset=64  <-- unexpected nonzero
hex dump (page=118 @ off=0): 3f 8a 21 ... 5a | actual tokens: <B's trailing chunk>
``` 

liam: That "start_offset=64" is the smell. We expect pages to be aligned to block boundaries after eviction/reshuffle. Could be an off-by-one in page compaction or reuse path.

sasha: Does this only show up with the vector-quantized kernel? Kernel selection sometimes switches to the 'fast-path' integer kernel that does smaller block writes; maybe we wrote a partial block and re-used it.

maya: Good point — I toggled kernel selection to force fp16, and repro rate dropped to ~0.0. With int8 fast-path it's ~0.02% per request set.

ron: Can you get a memory/profiling snapshot? I want to rule out stale refs preventing zeroing.

maya: Profile + heap dump attached (trimmed). Observations:
- memory grows with conversation length and doesn't fully drop after conversation end
- PageRef refcounts drop to 0 but BlockHeader->start_offset still points inside page
- gc::free_pages called but page remains in free list with stale header

maya: ```
# simplified stack
kv::evict_page(page=118)
kv::write_page(page=118, start_offset=64, len=4096)
kv::release_page(page=118) -> put_in_freelist
serve::acquire_free_page() -> returned page=118 with stale start_offset=64
```

alex: Looks like freelist reuse without clearing transient metadata. Two possible causes:
 1) eviction path doesn't reset BlockHeader.start_offset
 2) atomic race where writer sets start_offset then crash/abort and freelist reuses the page

sasha: There's also a tricky case: we purposely leave start_offset to speed up reuse when the next write is similar size. But that optimization assumes single-tenant or strict per-request ownership. For multi-tenant we must zero on release or guard reuse with an epoch check.

liam: Agree. For correctness we need to either zero metadata on release or stamp with epoch that acquire verifies.

maya: Drafted minimal patch: on release -> BlockHeader.start_offset = 0; BlockHeader.epoch = 0; atomic_thread_fence(seq_cst). Simple but adds small overhead to eviction path.

maya: ```cpp
void release_page(Page* p) {
  // clear transient metadata to avoid cross-request leakage
  p->header.start_offset = 0;
  p->header.valid_len = 0;
  p->header.epoch = 0;
  std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
  freelist.push(p);
}
```

ron: That will fix correctness. We should also add an acquire-time assert: if p->header.epoch != 0 and p->header.epoch != current_epoch then log and zero before use. Safety net.

sasha: Also add unit test that reuses freed pages across threads and checks for stale tokens. And add a perf microbenchmark — we expect ~0.5% slower evict path but no impact to steady-state throughput for long-running servers.

alex: Can we canary this change? I want to measure perf delta and watch for regressions in latency p95.

maya: I'll push branch and open PR. CI passed locally. Patch: rwd/infra#5123. Will run canary on prod-nyc with 5% traffic and extra verification that no cross-session tokens are emitted.

ci-bot: CI run for rwd/infra#5123 — tests: unit=✓, integration=✓, perf-smoke=✓ (local perf delta: -0.3% evict path). Merge blocked until canary verified.

liam: Also add a short-lived trace that records page header before/after release so we can replay if it reappears in canary.

maya: Canary deployed to prod-nyc (5%) with trace enabled. Will report in ~2h. :crossed_fingers: 

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started — service=runtime-prod-nyc, tag=v2.14.3+fix-kv-metadata, traffic=5%.

(2h later)

maya: Canary report: 24h-equivalent of requests sampled in 2h. No cross-session token leaks observed in traces. Latency p95 unchanged within noise. Memory stable. Looks good.

ron: Great. Let's merge with follow-ups: unit test, epoch-hash safety net, and a changelog note about disabling the old reuse micro-optimization.

alex: Merge done. Rollout to 100% scheduled in 30m.

deploy-bot: Rollout to 100% started — service=runtime-prod-nyc, tag=v2.14.3+fix-kv-metadata.

rachel: Thanks everyone. Big win — this was a sneaky correctness bug that could've leaked data across sessions. Keep an eye on canary traces for one more day.

maya: Will monitor. If anything else crops up I'll open a follow-up, but this fixed the repro locally too. :white_check_mark:
